scenes.heading: Handling clients who want unlimited revisions

sents.d: Handling clients who want unlimited revisions
'Unlimited revisions' in your contract is an invitation for the project to never end.

A specific number of revision rounds, defined in the contract before work starts, protects both you and the client — it gives them a clear structure to give focused feedback within, and protects your time from an open-ended back-and-forth.

When a client asks for 'just one more small change' past the agreed rounds, treating it consistently (a small per-round fee, or simply a polite reminder of the agreed scope) works better than making silent exceptions, which trains clients to expect unlimited free changes.

Most revision problems actually come from unclear direction upfront, not difficult clients — a structured brief and a clear first draft that matches it reduces the number of rounds needed far more than a strict revision policy alone.

take: Agree on rounds, enforce them kindly, and start with a strong brief.
